episodes.171136: Heavy rain from a good monsoonal push, caused flash flooding in eastern Nevada.
episodes.171243: High pressure remained centered over the Southern Plains which allowed for monsoon moisture to continue to stream into eastern Utah. This abundance of moisture resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain. Portions of San Juan County experienced flash flooding which led to significant road damage.
episodes.171449: A trough of tropical low pressure developed along the southern edge of a stalling cold front in the northwestern Gulf of Mexico. The circulation drifted ashore south of Corpus Christi and provided much needed rain to much of the Deep South Texas Ranch and Brush Country, with bands of torrential rain across the lower Rio Grande Valley.  It also spawned a waterspout and thunderstorm winds across the Lower Texas Coast on August 14th.
episodes.171640: With the monsoonal pattern continuing, heavy rainfall over the Mullen Fire Burn Scar area resulted in flooding of various streams and creeks. The Mullen Creek rose 3 feet at A Bar A Ranch in Carbon County from heavy rainfall upstream.
episodes.172340: A line of severe thunderstorms moved east across several counties in the Billings Forecast Area. The main impact from these thunderstorms was strong outflow wind gusts.
episodes.173262: Abundant moisture (PWATs 1.7-2.0) and instability (MUCAPE 2,000 J/kg) provided a favorable environment for strong to severe thunderstorms across south-central Arizona on the 14th. Daytime heating aided in thunderstorm development across the high terrain north of Phoenix before sending outflows traveling toward the south into the lower elevations. New thunderstorm development occurred along these outflows into the Valley where they produced damaging winds, dense blowing dust, and isolated flash flooding. Additional thunderstorm development occurred across southwest Arizona where better moisture allowed thunderstorms to be efficient rainfall producers, leading to multiple reports of flash flooding. No injuries were reported from this event.
episodes.173469: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines along with heavy rain which resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.173602: Much needed rainfall occurred over the Coastal Bend of south Texas on August 14th and 15th as an area of low pressure, that formed over the northwest Gulf of Mexico, moved inland. The low pressure area was close to becoming a tropical depression and the National Hurricane Center designated the system invest 98L. Bands of heavy tropical rainfall moved across Corpus Christi from the late morning into the middle of the afternoon. Locally heavy rainfall produced flooding of roadways across the city. Another band of showers moved across the same region during the early morning hours of the 15th. This caused flooding of roads again in Corpus Christi.
episodes.173625: Thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Isolated wind damage occurred in Tucson and Mescal with flash flooding in Oracle and along the Canada Del Oro Wash.
episodes.173631: Two rounds of thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast California, one round during the very early morning hours, between midnight through 4 am local time and another round during the mid to late afternoon hours. The early morning round was instigated by outflow boundaries that moved westward into southeast California from the decaying storm complex across southwest Arizona during the evening hours on the 12th. The environment was characterized by high moisture content (PWATs in excess of 2 inches) and moderate instability (MLCAPE of around 1000 J/KG). The mid to late afternoon round, was a more typical diurnal instigator and the environment once again was conducive, with very high moisture content (PWATs of 2+inches) and high instability (MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/KG).
episodes.173641: Diurnally and terrain induced thunderstorms developed across portions of southwest Arizona during the later afternoon and early evening hours. The environment was characterized by a very moist air mass (PWATs 2+ inches) and a highly unstable air mass (MLCAPE 1500+ J/KG). These favorable parameters resulted in the development of strong thunderstorm activity.
episodes.173731: An influx of high moisture values in a south-southwest wind flow pattern led to the development of numerous showers and thunderstorms over SE Florida.
episodes.173797: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Many storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173798: Persistent moist monsoonal flow fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173930: A decaying MCV remains over the eastern Mogollon Rim in the morning brought an area of showers and a few embedded thunderstorms remain. Otherwise, clearing skies allowed for increasing instability through the afternoon. This allowed strong thunderstorms to form that produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.173994: A trough of low pressure drifted from near the Louisiana Coast on August 12th to the Middle Texas coast by early on the 14th.  The trough, which included a mid-level circulation, moved across the coast near Riviera and would continue through Laredo between the 14th and 15th before moving northwest along the Rio Grande toward the Texas Big Bend region later on the 15th and 16th. ||Welcome rainfall of 3 to 7 inches during the day on the 14th helped quench the drought across the ranch country, and a small area from central Cameron county to southeast Willacy County also received an estimated 3 to 6 or more inches of rain. A torrential band may have dropped more than 8 inches along U.S. 83 in extreme northwest Zapata County late on August 15th.

events.narrative: Visibility was reported to be 1/2 mile from blowing dust.

Spotter reported via Facebook, that water running over US Highway 50, about 2 miles SE of Ruth. The observer sent a photo and estimated the water was about 6 to 12 inches over the road. Some sand and silt were noted in the photo as well.
White Hills Road was closed.
A car was swept off the road near Lincoln Dr and Congo Rd.
A thunderstorm microburst that moved through Winterhaven resulted in 49 downed power poles in the Quechan Tribe area. No injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour fell upstream to north of the Catalina Mountains in Pinal County. The Canada Del Oro Wash flowed over its banks south of Edwin Rd.
Flooding was reported on US-95 near Milepost 60. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported on US-95 near Milepost 72. No damages or injuries were reported.
Ogilby Road closed near the intersection with Sidewinder Road due to flooding. Vehicles were stranded between two washes pushing sediment and debris onto roadways. No injuries were reported.
Salem Church Road at Gemini Loop was closed due to flooding.
Highway 69 between Stephens Road and Hamilton Road was closed due to flooding.

Significant wind damage was observed in the Saddles of Joy property, located just southwest of Yuma Airport, from a thunderstorm microburst. Based on the images, large trees were uprooted, there was significant fencing damage, and destroyed sheds. A GoFundMe for 10K was set up to help with the damage cost. No injuries were reported.
Needles Highway was flooded.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in Oracle caused extensive street flooding throughout the town.
The stream gauge on Tonto Creek above Gun Creek showed almost a one foot rise in 30 minutes.

events.county: Waters From Baffin Bay To Pt Mansfield Tx Ext From 20 To 60Nm
events.narrative: Buoy 42020 recorded a measured wind gust of 37 knots the morning of August 14th as a thunderstorm associated with a trough of tropical low pressure moving ashore along trhe Coastal Bend south of Corpus Christi.
Report received from Mping of flooded streets with vehicles stranded along South Padre Island Drive between Rodd Field Road and Staples Street in Corpus Christi.
Post on Twitter was received of flooded waters on roadways reaching car bumpers from Flour Bluff to Rodd Field Road.
Rodd Field Road south of SPID became flooded and impassible with flood waters. Report by NWS employee of stalled cars with water up to the windows in spots.

events.county: Laguna Madre From Arroyo Colorado To 5Nm N Of Pt Mansfield Tx
events.narrative: A member of the public reported a waterspout near Port Mansfield. This was associated with a trough of low pressure that moved ashore over the Coastal Bend south of Corpus Christi on August 14th.
Report received through Mping of yards being flooded along with waters flooding a basement near Ennis Joslin Road to the west northwest of the Naval Air Station.

Lightning struck several units in the Players Place townhouse complex on Winners Circle in North Lauderdale during a heavy thunderstorm, igniting a fire which caused extensive roof damage. Four units were affected, two of which appeared to have sustained total damage. At least 12 people were displaced due to the damage. Time is based on National Lightning Detection network data which showed several lightning strikes in the immediate area. Damage totals are estimated.

Harbor Bridge construction project crews temporarily closed the Port Avenue and Nueces Bay Boulevard exits to Martin Luther King Drive and the northwest loop ramp connecting to southbound Crosstown Expressway in downtown Corpus Christi.
Emergency manager reported street flooding across the city from Flour Bluff to southeast Corpus Christi to Midtown to the Bayfront area.

Torrential rainfall, with local estimates of 2 or more inches per hour for two hours, produced street flooding from San Benito through La Tina Ranch, including along city and rural roads, with 1 to 2 feet of water on roads where the heaviest rainfall fell.  There were no reports of flooding of structures in these areas, and flood receded quickly after the slow moving band ended.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms washed out a large portion of State Road 211 near the intersection of Utah Highway 191. Significant water flowed across the highway. Vehicles were stranded in the area as a result.
A spotter reported major flooding around Kirkland due to very heavy rain.  That wash flows south then west toward Bagdad.
Several roads in and near Golden Valley were closed, and one swift water rescue was performed. A rain gauge measured 2.48 in one hour.
Flooding was reported on Highway 191 near Wide Ruin.
Hualapai Mountain Road was flooded near mile marker 5.
Power poles were reported down near Castle Hot Springs Road north of SR 74. No injuries were reported.

Mullen Creek, Savage Run, and Cottonwood Creek all flooded with the Mullen Creek rising 3 feet near the confluence with the North Platte River near A Bar A Ranch. Heavy rain was reported higher upstream over the Mullen Fire Burn Scar Area with 1 hour rainfall accumulation near 1 inch. A Bar A Ranch measured 0.58 inches of rainfall.

Heavy rain across the Rafael Fire (June 2021) caused a flash flood that entered the Verde River. The river gauge showed a 2.5 foot (600 CFS) increase in flow. The Verde River is a main stem river so flooding was not an issue once the flow reached that river.
A video showed multiple downed power poles along Patton Road near 259th Avenue with 60 mph winds recorded in the area. No injuries were reported.

A long travelling outflow boundary produced estimated gusts to around 35-40 mph, uprooting a large palo verde tree. The tree landed on a pickup truck, resulting in damage. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Hackberry Road was closed.
Heavy rain (2.40 inches in a short time) caused flooding in Model Creek and water was flowing over the Peeples Valley Road near the Model Creek School.
The Antelope Creek river gauge at Wickenburg Ranch started rising at 430 PM (around 349 CFS) and peaked at 1359 CFS at 455 PM MST.
Mineral Park Road was closed from Highway 93 to the mine entrance.
Chicken Springs Road was closed.
